newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-QUEENSLAND START LEGAL ACTION AGAINST SMITH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-QUEENSLAND START LEGAL ACTION AGAINST SMITH.

text.p: Queensland rugby union officials began legal action on Tuesday to prevent Australia test winger Damian Smith playing for a rival team.
Smith, who has two years remaining on his three-year contract with Queensland, has cited personal reasons for seeking a release to play for neighbouring New South Wales.
Queensland Rugby Union (QRU) chief executive Steve Thornton said attempts to settle the dispute had failed, forcing the ruling body to take the matter to the courts.
"We expect Damian to honour his commitment. It's a sad day but we are doing this in the interests of Australian rugby," Thornton said.
He said Smith had begun training with New South Wales in Sydney in preparation for this season's southern hemisphere Super 12 competition involving sides from Australia, South Africa and New Zealand.
"New South Wales' refusal to acknowledge our contract and Damian's refusal to even talk to us left us with no alternative," Thornton said.
He said the Queensland union had taken out an injunction which "seeks to enforce Smith's obligation not to play for another provincial team".
